projects.name: Order & Inventory API · Java Backend
projects.stack: Java 21 · Spring Boot 3 · Spring Data JPA · Spring Security · PostgreSQL · Docker
projects.summary: Personal backend concept for a retail ordering system: secure REST APIs, transactional inventory and reliable request retries using Java and Spring Boot.
bullets: API design: Controller–Service–Repository layers, DTOs, Jakarta Bean Validation, pagination and centralized exception handling with stable HTTP error contracts.
Persistence design: Spring Data JPA with PostgreSQL, schema migrations using Flyway, database constraints and indexes; fetch strategies to avoid N+1 queries.
Inventory design: @Transactional order creation and conditional stock updates; zero updated rows trigger a business exception and rollback.
Security design: Spring Security with JWT authentication, role-based authorization and BCrypt password hashing; secrets supplied through environment variables.
Retry design: unique idempotency keys prevent duplicate orders; reusing a key with a different payload is rejected; notifications are decoupled through a proposed transactional outbox.
Verification plan: JUnit 5/Mockito unit tests, PostgreSQL integration tests with Testcontainers, concurrent-order test cases, OpenAPI docs, Docker Compose and health checks.
projects.problem: Concurrent purchases, network timeouts and repeated requests can cause overselling, duplicate orders or notifications for failed transactions.
projects.approach: A modular Spring Boot API with explicit transaction boundaries, PostgreSQL constraints, conditional inventory updates and idempotent order creation. A transactional outbox is proposed for post-commit notifications.
projects.focus: Personal project concept, not a completed or production-deployed application. The architecture and feature list describe the proposed implementation.
